paragraphs: Modern camouflage is designed against a camera as much as against an eye, which is why the patterns became pixelated: broken edges defeat the shape recognition that a human brain and a sensor both rely on. The cut of the uniform follows the body armour it is worn under.
The uniform is light at 17,761 polygons and 19,022 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, suited to crowds and background characters. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $79 it suits game characters, defence and film costume work, training material, apparel visualisation and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

A car hauler is a puzzle solved in steel. Ramps, tilting decks and hydraulic posts exist so that vehicles of different heights can be interleaved nose to tail, because the trailer is paid by the car and not by the tonne.

The model holds 683,592 polygons and 702,184 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 11 maps all at 4096x4096, in a generic scheme carrying no branding. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $79 it suits transport and logistics visualisation, automotive delivery scenes, fleet mockups, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2019.

A pump on a trailer is the answer to a problem that moves. Flooded sites, temporary bypasses, irrigation and construction dewatering all need serious flow for a few days in a place that has no power, which is why the engine and the pump travel together.

The model holds 150,610 polygons and 152,146 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and carries StemCell certification. Rigged builds are offered separately, including native rigs for Cinema 4D and Maya.
At $79 it suits construction and utilities visualisation, equipment marketing, emergency and flood response material, training, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2025.

A disintegrator breaks material apart by impact rather than by cutting, and the separator behind it sorts what comes out by size and weight. Together they are the front end of almost every recycling and minerals process there is.
The model holds 592,204 polygons and 315,757 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and carries StemCell certification for use across engines and renderers.
At $79 it suits industrial and processing visualisation, equipment marketing, recycling and minerals presentation, training material, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2023.

Formalwear tailored for a shorter body is not a scaled down suit, and pretending otherwise is how most digital wardrobes get it wrong. Proportion, lapel width and the position of the waist all have to be redrawn, which is why a purpose built garment is worth having.
The garment is very light at 3,481 polygons and 3,704 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in beige, so it costs almost nothing in a scene. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $79 it suits character wardrobe work, game and animation assets, apparel and retail visualisation, film costume previsualisation and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

The scissor lift is one of the neatest mechanisms in construction: a stack of crossed arms that turns a short hydraulic push into a long vertical rise, with no cables and nothing to fall out of alignment. An engine powered one goes outside, onto ground a battery machine could not cross.

The model holds 103,347 polygons and 106,501 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 13 maps, 3 at 8192x8192 and 10 at 4096x4096. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $79 it suits construction and access equipment visualisation, equipment marketing, training and safety material, site scenes and game environments. On sale since 2016.

Everest is not the most difficult mountain to climb, and it is not the tallest measured from base to summit. What it is, unarguably, is the highest point on the surface of the planet, and that single fact has determined everything that has happened to it.
The model is light at 47,956 polygons and 47,835 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, suited to wide scenes and mapping work, and carries StemCell certification.

At $79 it suits geographic and landscape visualisation, documentary and education material, news graphics, mapping and terrain presentation, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2025.

The industrial shed is the most built structure of the last century and the least designed. A portal frame, a roof, cladding and a door big enough for a lorry: it is architecture reduced to enclosing volume at the lowest possible cost.

The model is extremely light at 4,880 polygons and 5,339 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 5 maps all at 4096x4096, so whole industrial estates can be built from it. It carries StemCell certification.
At $79 it suits urban and industrial visualisation, city and aerial scenes, infrastructure presentation, film backgrounds, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2020.

Showing the reproductive organs together with the kidneys is a deliberate teaching choice: the two systems are neighbours, share the same developmental origin, and a great many clinical questions turn on the relationship between them.

The model is very light at 7,368 polygons and 7,394 vertices, built in quads only with overlapping UVs, so it runs in a browser or on a tablet without difficulty. It is built to CheckMate specification.

At $79 it suits medical education and patient explanation, gynaecology and urology material, pharmaceutical visualisation, apps and interactive learning, and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

A flat top barge has no hold and no sides, which makes it the most flexible deck on the water. Modules, cranes, pipe and whole buildings ride on top of it, strapped or welded down, because there is nothing in the way.
The model holds 342,852 polygons and 358,194 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 13 maps all at 4096x4096. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $79 it suits marine and offshore visualisation, heavy transport and logistics presentation, port and industrial scenes, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2018.

A hippo does not swim, it walks along the bottom and pushes off. Floating is the pose most people picture, with the eyes, ears and nostrils in a line just above the surface, which is exactly where they sit so the animal can breathe, hear and watch without surfacing.
The model is supplied with fur, in the floating pose, and carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $79 it suits wildlife and nature visualisation, documentary and education work, zoo and safari imagery, game environments, advertising and editorial illustration. On sale since 2016.

A folding grill is designed around the walk back to the car. It has to pack flat, weigh nothing worth complaining about, and still hold a fire steady enough to cook over, which is a harder set of compromises than the price of these things suggests.
The model holds 119,962 polygons and 120,969 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplied with the fire. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $79 it suits outdoor and camping visualisation, product and retail imagery, advertising and lifestyle scenes, film sets, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

Naval dress uniform is one of the last places where rank is worn openly and read instantly. Every stripe, button and piece of braid carries specific information, which is why the design has changed so little: the garment is a document as much as clothing.
The uniform is very light at 5,835 polygons and 5,990 vertices in quads and tris with mixed UV layout, so it costs almost nothing in a crowd. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $79 it suits character wardrobe work, film and television costume, ceremonial and historical scenes, game characters, education material and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

Removing the mirror removed the last mechanical link between the lens and the photographer's eye, and everything about camera design changed as a result: shorter bodies, shorter flange distances, and lenses that could finally be computed without a swinging mirror in the way.

The model holds 59,665 polygons and 61,238 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 29 maps, 25 at 4096x4096, 2 at 2048x2048 and 2 at 1024x1024, which is enough for close product work. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $79 it suits product and technology visualisation, e-commerce and catalogue imagery, advertising, studio and desk scenes, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2017.
